code.install: Set up the isolated motion worker in the ComfyUI_VNCCS_Utils folder: 'motion_worker/install.sh hymotion' then 'motion_worker/run.sh hymotion' (Windows: install.bat / run.bat; Docker: docker compose -f motion_worker/docker-compose.yml --profile hymotion up -d --build). See motion_worker/README.md. Clone the model code too: 'git lfs install && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-Motion-1.0 models/text_to_motion/code/HY-Motion-1.0'.

requirements.notes: Text-only: the motion cannot start from a given pose, so Pose Studio applies its movement on top of the current pose. The Qwen3-8B text encoder is most of the download.

setup.label: Isolated motion worker
setup.detail: The model runs in its own venv next to this extension, so ComfyUI's packages are never changed and your other workflows keep running. In the custom_nodes/ComfyUI_VNCCS_Utils folder run the command once (it creates the venv), then keep the worker running next to ComfyUI. Windows (also ComfyUI portable): motion_worker\install.bat hymotion, then motion_worker\run.bat hymotion. No Python on the machine? Install uv first; the script then downloads Python 3.11 into the venv by itself. Optional, if you already use Docker: docker compose -f motion_worker/docker-compose.yml --profile hymotion up -d --build

setup.label: HY-Motion code
setup.detail: Clone the repository into ComfyUI's models folder. Run the command from the ComfyUI folder. The worker installs what it needs; do not install the repository's requirements.txt into ComfyUI.
setup.command: git lfs install && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-Motion-1.0 models/text_to_motion/code/HY-Motion-1.0
